observations: Live BCCI Ranji Trophy · Plate tournament actually DID match a tournament_master row (category=BCCI, name exact match). Task hypothesis said master_matched=false; in reality master_matched=true but with all null DOB/gender/medical fields, so engine returns all players as eligible (functionally equivalent to no enforcement). This is correct behaviour per the engine spec (rule 1-4 all pass on null master fields).
Endpoint returns 200 with counts {total:0, eligible:0, ineligible:0} when no players are in DB (as expected — only 1 tournament, 0 players seeded).
critical_code_review_comments: core/tournament_eligibility.py: _player_dob has a subtle bug — for non-string dob values it returns None on first key even if second key holds a valid string (the walrus-like assignment sets v=None when player.get(k) is not a string, skipping the truthy check). In practice players store dob as ISO string so no impact, but tighten to `v = player.get(k); if isinstance(v,str) and v.strip(): return v.strip()`.
routes/tournament_eligibility.py: body_id regex match uses `{body_code}$` without escaping — a body_code containing regex metachars could throw. Consider re.escape.
seed_data_creation: Pytest fixture seeded 1 tournament + 3 players (auto cleanup after run).
